abstract: Small Alarmone Synthetase-related proteins (SASs) belong to the RelA/SpoT Homolog (RSH) protein superfamily, sharing an SYNTH domain with long, multidomain RSHs Rel, RelA, and SpoT. Some SASs are secreted effectors in antagonism, while others are toxin-antitoxin system toxins, some of which function in phage defense. Here, we analyze SAS proteins using phylogeny, domain architecture, genomic neighborhoods and structural predictions. SASs often carry diverse accessory domains, and commonly associate with conserved partner proteins with which they are often predicted to form complexes. Multiple SAS subfamilies co-localize with phage defense genes, and some are frequently encoded on predicted prophages, consistent with involvement in defense against, and conflict among mobile genetic elements. Recurrent association with partner domain folds and parallel evolution of embedding within larger systems highlight the multi-level evolutionary plasticity and functional diversification of SASs and suggest that catalytic activity is regulated in a variety of ways across the SAS family tree.
